USAGE GUIDE - FUEL STATION
1. DAILY WORK - Operations > Shifts: open the shift (Open), enter the closing index of each nozzle, the payments and the shop sales, count the banknotes and coins (Cash Control tab), then Close. - Operations > Deliveries: receive the fuel in the tanks. Operations > Tank Dips: compare the measured level to the stock. - Stock > Tank Levels / Low Tanks: monitor the tanks. Reports > Fuel Sales: sales by day, station and fuel. - Quantities are in gallons.
2. DISPENSING AUTHORIZATIONS Tryton requests and records. The certified controller of the station decides physically whether a pump may dispense. Tryton is never connected to the pump control circuits: a middleware, validated by the equipment manufacturer and the authorized installer, carries the authorizations to the controller. Flow: 1. Operator: Operations > Dispensing Authorizations > New. Choose the station, the pump, the nozzle (it imposes the fuel), the limit (maximum quantity or maximum amount), the customer and/or the vehicle. Save: the authorization is Pending. 2. Manager: Operations > Authorizations to Approve > Approve (or Reject). The approver must not be the requester. Tryton keeps the user, the time and the authorized limits. The authorization then expires after the validity delay of the station. 3. Middleware: reads the approved authorizations, gives them to the controller (Transmitted), the controller confirms (Confirmed), then sends back the quantity, the amount and the transaction reference. 4. Tryton compares the result with the authorization: if it is correct the authorization is Completed, the stock is moved and, with the sale module, the sale and the invoice are created. Any difference (limit exceeded, late or repeated result, expiry) puts it in Discrepancy for a manager to resolve; nothing is hidden. Rules: single use, one live authorization per pump, short expiry, quantity or amount ceiling, pump and fuel imposed, cancellation controlled (after transmission only a manager can request it and the controller must acknowledge), full audit log in the Audit Log tab, no authorization when the communication with the controller is lost or blocked.
3. WHO DOES WHAT - Fuel Station: operators (request, shifts, deliveries, dips). - Fuel Authorization Manager: approve, reject, resolve discrepancies, request cancellation after transmission. - Fuel Middleware: technical user of the middleware only. - Fuel Station Administration: configuration.
4. WHEN SOMETHING GOES WRONG - "Communication lost": the middleware sent no signal within the timeout of the station. Check the middleware and the controller; the pumps are not affected, they simply stay under the control of the controller. - Authorization Expired: request a new one. - Discrepancy: open the audit log, check the controller records, then Resolve with a note.
